findings.summary: Accepted the security-sensitive implementation across every named concern: toLogicalKey, assertSafeKey, filesystemPathFor, deleteCapture, canonical forward-slash keys, legacy backslash keys, mixed separators, traversal, percent-encoded traversal, Windows absolute paths, drive-relative paths, UNC paths, POSIX absolute paths, root containment, tenant crossover, storage-deletion failure and encrypted biometric retention.
Normalise-then-validate ordering accepted as the control against a backslash traversal defeating a check written for forward slashes. assertSafeKey runs after toLogicalKey and never before it.

Root containment accepted as retained defence in depth. The check is byte-identical to before and is now unreachable through the public API because a key that passes assertSafeKey cannot escape the root. Recorded as a backstop rather than claimed as an active control.
CONV-003 examined explicitly, as the second reviewer is required to. Dispositioned separately as ACCEPTED_RISK under the Application Security decision of the same date.

notes: This is the security-literate second human code review R4 requires. With REV-0002 it completes CONV-001.

PROVENANCE. The decision was made by a human, GreenArrow-7, and given explicitly in session on 2026-09-08 as a Security-Literate Qualified Human Code Reviewer APPROVE on SPEC-0005. An AI agent transcribed it. The agent did not make the decision and does not hold the reviewer role.

The same human supplied both code-review decisions. R4 requires two reviewers, one security-literate; whether one person may hold both slots is a question for the standard, and it is flagged here rather than assumed away. The record shows one actorId on both reviews so that a later auditor can see it plainly and judge it.
Scope: the code review only. NOT convergence acceptance, and NOT production, staging or deployment approval.
